desired_count_changes.definition: Saved metrics.resources.replica_churn: changes in sampled desired replica counts. This is not a count of Kubernetes HPA event-log records or completed resizes.

e2e_run_p95_ms.definition: Run-level 95th percentile of per-tick p95 latencies. Tick latencies use successful requests; a tick with no successful requests records zero. This is not the p95 of pooled requests.

overhead_replica_seconds_per_hour.definition: Overhead replica-seconds above one minimum replica, divided by configured workload duration in hours.

tick_slo_violation_fraction.definition: Fraction of workload ticks whose successful-request p95 exceeds 200 ms; zero-success ticks have p95 zero and therefore do not count as violations.

qualifications: Stored-result reproduction only: no independent raw-run rescore, new experiment, or scientific replication.
The batches are separate cohorts and must not be pooled.
Means are over admitted runs within each method and workload pattern.
Latency and tick-violation ordering can differ; neither metric establishes general superiority or fault resilience.
Reported Welch intervals are copied from saved summaries, unpaired and unadjusted; shared-host and block dependence are not modelled.

Definition-reference hashes identify code inspected during export; they do not prove which code bytes executed historically. The 200 ms tick threshold and run-p95 definition were checked against every retained workload trace.
Corrected-point versus tuned CPU HPA fails the recorded cost criterion on pattern D, despite the overall three-of-four-pattern rule passing. Its cost-difference 95% interval spans zero.
Against tuned CPU HPA, the corrected point controller has higher mean p95 but lower tick-violation share on pattern C; pattern D has lower mean p95 but higher tick-violation share.
The stored cost criterion allows at most 5% greater mean overhead than the reference; a pass does not mean strictly cheaper.

The recorded service criterion requires complete per-run values. Mean p95 must be no greater than the reference, or have a recorded two-sided Welch p-value above 0.05, or be within +5% of the reference. Mean tick-violation fraction and request-error fraction must each be no more than reference +0.03, and no candidate run may have zero successful requests.

The recorded overall rule requires an eligible completed cohort, enough valid replicates, and cost plus service criteria passing on at least three of four patterns. The saved verdict is PASS with three of four patterns passing. These decisions are copied, not independently recomputed here; a non-significant p-value does not establish equivalence.
These frozen-interval and corrected-point configurations have interval recalibration, coverage monitoring and escalation disabled; they do not measure online interval repair.
No retained checkpoint-hash manifest is supplied for this batch; model configuration is retained, but historical checkpoint bytes are not independently verified here.
